digest.component_or_area: RP-04 secrets and authentication architecture research
propositions: Rebar must support provider-native authentication (Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Git, GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Jira) across local, CI, and AWS-hosted environments without weakening SDK-native refresh, workload identity, or credential rotation

Current _bridge_runner propagates full parent environment including unrelated Jira/LLM/cloud credentials to reconciler and ticket delivery, creating unintended credential exposure across adapter boundaries

Deployment must resolve external secret stores (SSM, keyring, cloud secrets) before process startup; Rebar consumes only provider-native auth capabilities and narrowly scoped static carriers at adapter boundaries without introducing a universal secret broker or automatic hot-rotation cache

Operation-certificate signing accepts exactly one of REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (file, preferred) or multiline REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY (env) at startup; static credentials rotate only via restart/redeploy, not in-process polling or hot-reload

Trusted same-capability subprocesses inherit ambient environment for compatibility; Rebar overlays Rebar-materialized static values only onto the owning child and removes exact unrelated adapter secret names from sibling processes without mutating global os.environ

Pydantic SecretStr/SecretBytes wrap unavoidable static credentials in provider-specific non-serializable containers, excluded from repr/comparison/hashing/caching/fingerprints, with explicit unwrap only inside the sending adapter
